subject: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details
messages:
From: Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: sig-assess@veritas-audit.com
Date: 2027-06-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Hi Irene,

Following up on the SIG questionnaire items around Secure SDLC: we need provenance artifacts showing code review and change-management controls for the past 12 months for the services used by Moneta Financial (model ingestion pipeline and inference gateway). Specifically please provide or indicate where we can retrieve:

- PR review policy and a sample of PR approvals (including reviewers, timestamps, and merge audit).
- CI/CD pipeline configuration and evidence of pipeline gating (test/scan steps, who can bypass).
- Secrets handling: ephemeral credentialing, KMS usage, and any documented rotation procedures + a sample KMS audit entry.
- Change ownership chronology for a recent rollout (canary + full rollout), including who approved, what run IDs correspond to the merge, and rollback capability.

We don't need full logs for all runs, but a handful of representative artifacts (CSV/Exports, a couple of run IDs, and a KMS audit sample) should be sufficient to validate controls. If anything is sensitive, please flag and we'll accept redacted outputs.

Deadline: can you confirm availability to provide these artifacts by COB 2027-06-14?

Thanks,
Alex Byrne
Senior Assessor, Veritas Audit

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a representative bundle by the 14th. High-level notes here and attachments to follow in separate message:

- PR reviews: GitHub branch-protection + required-code-review rules in place for 18 months. I'll attach a control matrix and an export of merge approval events for the last 6 months.
- CI/CD: we use GitHub Actions for unit/integration and an internal runner for deployment gates. The pipeline enforces smoke tests + static analysis; only service owners can approve production deployments via a review app.
- Secrets & KMS: all production secrets are stored in the customer KMS-backed vault (CloudKMS). Ephemeral service tokens are issued by the runners for short-lived deploy tasks; rotation policy is quarterly for long-lived keys.
- Change ownership & rollouts: we follow a canary -> scaled -> full rollout pattern with automatic rollback on error thresholds. I'll include the canary roll log and a sample KMS audit entry.

I'll attach: control-matrix.csv and merge-approval-exports.zip in the next message. Jordan, can you drop the PR policy and CI config snippets? Kimberly, FYI in case you want to add the rollout chronology note.

Irene
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-09T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Attaching the technical snippets you asked for. Quick clarifications in-line: 

- PR gating: we require two reviewers for changes touching 'services/*' and an automated approval block if any code-scan fails. The team can configure exceptions, but exceptions are logged and time-limited (see pr-policy.md).
- CI pipeline: the deploy job is gated behind a manual approval step labeled 'prod-deploy-authorize' which is only actionable by the service owner and the oncall-sre role. The YAML snippet (ci-pipeline-config.yaml) shows the job gating and the list of checks.
- Bypass and emergency rollback: bypass is supported via an emergency runbook but requires a JIRA ticket and dual-approval (oncall + engineering lead) — we export those tickets for audit as part of merge-approval-exports.zip.

Attachments in this message: pr-policy.md, ci-pipeline-config.yaml

—Jordan
Staff Engineer, Platform

From: Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T08:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Thanks Jordan — that helps. Couple of quick clarifying asks before we close the loop:

1) For ephemeral credentials: can you provide a sample KMS audit entry that shows issuance and revocation events tied to a pipeline run ID (we asked for a sample KMS audit entry previously but want to make sure it includes run correlation).
2) For the change that triggered the incident the Moneta team flagged in late Apr (ticket MON-4689), can you provide the PR number, merge timestamp, and the CI run ID that corresponds to the production rollout? We only need the single PR/rollout trace for that incident.

If you can drop those two items (kms-audit-sample.txt + canary-rollout-log.csv with the PR/run mapping), that should complete our evidence set.

Alex

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Alex — attaching the requested items for MON-4689 trace and a KMS audit sample. Notes:

- PR #: 4821 — merged 2027-04-27T03:12:14Z. The GitHub merge_event export is included in merge-approval-exports.zip.
- CI run ID: gha-run-20270427-8f3b2 — see canary-rollout-log.csv for the canary phases and the timestamp mapping to the run ID. The canary experienced elevated error rates at phase 3 and triggered an automated rollforward after a 12-minute mitigation window; rollback was not required because the fix was in the subsequent patch (PR 4834).
- KMS audit sample: kms-audit-sample.txt contains an issuance event for ephemeral token svc-deploy-20270427 and a revocation event after 15 minutes; entries include the pipeline run ID as a free-form field.

Attachments: canary-rollout-log.csv, kms-audit-sample.txt

Let me know if you'd like additional CSV columns (we can export the reviewer emails column), otherwise this should close it out.

Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Byrne <alex@veritas-audit.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-11T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance and change ownership details

Received — thanks all. The PR/merge/run mapping and the KMS sample look good. One small follow-up: can you paste the exact CI run URL for gha-run-20270427-8f3b2 (no need to export logs) so we can reference it in our findings? After that we'll mark the item resolved.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Byrne
Senior Assessor, Veritas Audit
